atomicity.reason: One obligation: open the contactors when a valid cell voltage is outside the window.

comprehensibility.reason: The limits are not literals but variant references, so the body as authored (and as the audit shows it) does not carry the numbers; a reader needs the active variant data file to know the window.
comprehensibility.suggestion: Name the default profile and its values in prose next to the references, e.g. '(2.50 V to 4.25 V in the NMC profile)', so the requirement reads on its own.

feasibility.reason: Cell-voltage supervision against fixed limits is the standard reaction; contradicts nothing else stated.

parent_fit.reason: Implements the story's 'leaves its safe voltage window' for the voltage dimension, per cell, exactly as the story frames it.

unambiguity.reason: Per-cell application and the validity precondition are both explicit; one reading.

verifiability.reason: In any given build the window resolves to two concrete limits (2.50 V and 4.25 V in the default NMC profile), so a bench test is unambiguous per variant.

summary: The 150 % formulation keeps one obligation across chemistries; its cost is that the source text no longer states the numbers, which the body should compensate for.
